scope: Physical route review, not new connectivity evidence. X1 serves the matrix/LEDs; XT1 is the host cable. Reference endpoints are targets for tracing, not observed attachments.

crossSideSearch.scope: Search localization only. Fits share R4.2 anchors; agreement is a sensitivity check, not independent evidence. Top DIP landmarks are lead observations, not verified hole centres. No copper or via assignment is qualified.

crossSideStop.observation: The projected location falls beneath the resistor body in the primary top photo. The top counterpart and outgoing copper cannot be identified directly there.

cases.title: Serial clock: driver to filter to host cable
cases.finding: The R10.1 branch reaches a solder eye beneath R9.5. A local resistor-bank fit supports a downstream eye correspondence beside R9.7, and an observed outer underside lane continues from there toward an eye near R4.1. Resistor bodies hide the intervening top spans; the new observations remain electrically unassigned. A1, winding and host-cable attachments are not closed.
alternatives: Reference path reaches A1:2 and L1.1:1 through hidden copper.
The apparent top/bottom stop correspondence is wrong; the visible branch requires a different continuation. This is a geometric alternative, not a replacement net assignment.
cases.nextDeskWork: Resolve the hidden bank spans and the upper-eye continuation near R4.1 before assigning the outer lane to clock. The exposed bent corridor stops before the capacitor-side copper; resolve both its upper-eye join and its hidden capacitor-side continuation. The wider mixed fit fails held-out checks and must not assign an LF joint.
cases.decisiveObservation: An uninterrupted path, including any confirmed layer transition, from R10.1:2 to A1:2 and the identified L1.1 input. Separately identify both winding ends and the cable-side connection to XT1:B2.
cases.doNotInfer: The former A1:13 conflict came from a rejected projection. It is not a measured short, and the surviving local segment does not identify the hidden A1 pin.

crossSideStop.observation: The projected location falls beneath the resistor body in the primary top photo. The top counterpart and outgoing copper cannot be identified directly there.

cases.title: Serial data: driver to filter to host cable
cases.finding: The R10.2 underside branch stops beneath R7. A local R4.2/R8 fit checked against R7 narrows the search; exposed top spans lie between R7/R4.2 and R4.2/R6.1. Bodies still hide the joins, so the spans remain unassigned.
alternatives: The solder eye continues to the reference A1:4/L1.4:1 network.
A nearby top-side eye or winding lead is being mistaken for the counterpart; preserve the open span until independently matched.
cases.nextDeskWork: Resolve the R7 layer transition and hidden joins under R4.2 and R6.1 in path-tracing.json. The registered comparison corridor confirms visibility limits, not primary continuity; continue toward L1 only from a supported downstream eye.
cases.decisiveObservation: Identify the actual winding input and output joints, then establish the R10.2:2–A1:4–L1.4:1 and L1.4:2–XT1:A1 spans independently.
cases.doNotInfer: Cable wire colour and spatial proximity do not establish a terminal number or which ferrite winding is L1.4.

cases.title: Clock strobe input: distinguish CPU WR from RD
cases.finding: The reference supports WR, while a published comparison uses RD. An observed underside lane links terminal candidates near A4 and A6; the corresponding top track enters beneath A6. Local A6 registration supports a candidate outside the anchor hull. Neither CPU attachment is established.
alternatives: A1:1 connects to A5:22 (WR), as in the reference.
A1:1 connects to A5:21 (RD), as in the published comparison.
The terminal correspondence is still wrong or incomplete; neither candidate is established.
cases.nextDeskWork: Reverse inspection of both CPU candidates stops at covered pin exits. Resolve the A4/A6 layer transitions and the hidden A5/A6 route; the separate land beyond the CPU row is not either CPU joint. Neither WR nor RD is excluded by the current photos.
cases.decisiveObservation: A complete photographed route or distinguishable unpowered resistance readings from A1:1 to A5:21 and A5:22, with probe locations recorded.
cases.doNotInfer: A successful S600 simulation of the WR reference does not determine the specimen's physical attachment.

cases.title: X1 matrix connector: retain the constrained row order
cases.finding: The LED attachments constrain the far row, and the COL11 attachment constrains the near row independently. Their combined result already resolves the reference row order conditionally; it is not an open whole-connector reversal problem.
alternatives: Retain the sole row mapping consistent with all recorded attachments.
Reopen that mapping only if a specific attachment or component identity is disproved.
cases.nextDeskWork: Use these independently constrained contacts as registration checks while resolving the remaining contact and neighbouring output routes.
cases.decisiveObservation: Independently confirm the three recorded endpoints; preserve the intermediate COL11 solder eye without inventing a top-side branch.
cases.doNotInfer: X1 is not the serial host connector. Its row ordering does not identify XT1 cable terminals.

cases.title: X1 A8: classify the schematic-omitted contact
cases.finding: A physical contact position exists in the constrained row order, but no X1:A8 pin occurs in the reference netlist. It remains visual geometry only.
alternatives: Unused contact with no electrical connection.
Specimen-specific connection omitted from the reference.
Apparent attachment is opposite-side copper or an obscured neighbouring lead.
cases.nextDeskWork: Inspect the marked far-row eighth lead and underside joint in the primary photos, then compare the mating-face and bent-lead views without equating their coordinates with the primary specimen.
cases.decisiveObservation: A visible complete attachment or a recorded contact-to-pad resistance map that distinguishes an unused contact from a connected one. An obscured trace is not evidence of disconnection.
cases.doNotInfer: Do not create a numbered native pad or assign a net simply to fill the missing schematic position.
